output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. Other groups look normal, so general market mobility and the firm-wide hours target don't explain this group. Pay is unlikely to be the main driver, because the associates not on Kestrel were paid the same and almost all stayed. The records can't separate two explanations. All Kestrel associates worked under Dorian Faulk, and Faulk supervises no other matter, so the punishing workload and his supervision style are completely entangled. Survey comments point to both. I'm moderately sure about the concentration and not sure at all about workload versus supervision. Don't announce the £12k payment and close the review. It would probably miss the cause and leave the Kestrel associates still at risk. Commission the confidential outside interviews (about £9k, three weeks), structured to separate supervision from workload, and ask leavers and current Kestrel associates. While that runs, protect the remaining Kestrel associates, as a stopgap, with extra review capacity or a supervision check. Also start recording matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting.
